question.problem:
The Cartesian equation of the circle defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=\frac{5}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -2,\,y=\frac{5}{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -3,\,0\le \theta <2\pi 
$$

is given by

$(x\,+$
{{field-1}}$)^{2}+(y\,+$
{{field-2}}$)^{2}=$
{{field-3}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the circle, we need to eliminate the parameter $\theta .$ We can do this using the Pythagorean theorem.

By isolating the $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ term in the $x$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2 & =\frac{5}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{6}{5}(x+2) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{36}{25}(x+2)^{2} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

By isolating the $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ term in the $y$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+3 & =\frac{5}{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{6}{5}(y+3) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{36}{25}{(y+3)}^{2} & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations and using ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{36}{25}(x+2)^{2}+\frac{36}{25}{(y+3)}^{2} & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{36}{25}(x+2)^{2}+\frac{36}{25}{(y+3)}^{2} & =1 \\ (x+2)^{2}+{(y+3)}^{2} & =\frac{25}{36}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation is ${(x+2)}^{2}+{(y+3)}^{2}=\frac{25}{36}.$
